taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

finalText:
The sources I opened show no newer replacement for RFC 9110, which is the current HTTP Semantics specification (STD 97). Every code below is defined in section 15 of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. I read each section's text on that page.

**Cacheability rule.** The page says "Responses with status codes that are defined as heuristically cacheable (e.g., 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification)". Of the 12 codes you asked about, that list covers 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501. Each of those sections also says "A NNN response is heuristically cacheable". The sections for 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 say nothing about heuristic cacheability, and the same passage states "all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable", so I report them as false.

**Reason phrases.** RFC 9110 renamed some phrases compared with the older RFC 7231 wording. The current phrases are 413 "Content Too Large" and 422 "Unprocessable Content". I did not open RFC 7231's text for this comparison, so the older names ("Payload Too Large", "Unprocessable Entity") come from my memory rather than from a page I read.

**Plan deviation.** The plan suggested checking the rfc-editor.org info page for "Obsoleted by". That URL returned a 404, so I used a search instead. The search results gave no sign of a successor.
